clue.text: Shot of rum lovely after some beer …

parts.note: a half is half a pint of beer, ordered in a British pub

indicators.note: rum is an old word for odd or strange, so the letters come out in a peculiar order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinker downs a nice tot of rum after a pint, the ellipsis leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink being ordered but signals the rearrangement; 'after' puts the beer first.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis or cricket, a ball struck just as it bounces up from the ground is a type of stroke.

clue.text: Show of devotion in acquiring a Golf

indicators.note: to acquire something is to take it into your possession, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: at home means in, as opposed to out
taken as written
G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone shows their devotion to the game by taking up golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as a plain preposition, but it stands for HOME, as in 'staying in'; A and G sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Homage is public respect or tribute paid to someone, a formal display of allegiance or reverence.

clue.text: News of US city trial

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A report on a court case in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a courtroom trial; here trial just means a test.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking 'what's the latest?' means asking for the most recent developments or updates.

clue.text: Maybe one out of three taking rough side, keeping right

parts.note: rough in the sense of coarse or crude

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a side or group within a party
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Perhaps a sporting team, one of three sides, with a rough player kept on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One out of three' sounds like picking one of three people, but it is the number one-third written as a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A vulgar fraction is a common fraction written with numerator over denominator, such as one-third, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Frolicking Mandela — it gets glossed over

indicators.note: frolicking is playing about friskily, so the letters jump around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, the rest of the fodder

explanation.surface: A playful picture of Nelson Mandela dancing, while some awkward fact is quietly ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glossed over' in the surface means ignored; as the definition it means literally given a glossy coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Laminated means covered with a thin protective layer, often shiny plastic, giving a glossy surface to card or paper.

clue.text: E.g. Marathon Man extremely cut up beginning to incite dissatisfaction

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards
cutting at the extremes trims away the outermost letter at each end

parts.note: a marathon man is an example of a runner

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of incite

explanation.surface: A long-distance runner, or the film Marathon Man, is cut up and stirs up discontent.
explanation.walkthrough: Marathon Man is a 1976 thriller film, but here it is just an example of a RUNNER; dropping both end letters leaves UNNE, which reads upwards as ENNU.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom and weariness, a general discontent with life, borrowed from French.

clue.text: .. possibly a pint and not quite tight?

parts.note: taken as written
'possibly' admits the jar need not be a pint

explanation.surface: Continuing from 1 Across: the drinker has had a pint and is not quite drunk yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' in the surface means drunk; in the definition it means firmly shut, as a door can be.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left ajar is slightly open rather than firmly closed, so it is not quite shut.

clue.text: Scrap plane, it's wobbling about

parts.note: a jet is a kind of plane

indicators.note: something wobbling is unsteady and shaky, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: An aircraft shaking about badly is fit only for the scrapheap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like part of 'wobbling about', but it is a separate piece meaning 'on the subject of'.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw away or discard, originally cargo dumped from a ship or aircraft.

clue.text: Turncoat betrayed a general's part in revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the letters run the other way
a part is only a section of the whole, so the letters come from inside the run of words

parts.note: the letters sit across the end of the first word, all of the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A traitor betrayed a general by playing his part in an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In revolution' suggests a political uprising, which fits the traitor, but it is the instruction to read the run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat is someone who deserts their side or cause for the opposition, exactly what a renegade does.

clue.text: Redundant counsellor confirms lunch perhaps with daughter Jordan?

parts.note: to back up a claim is to confirm it
having lunch is an example of eating
D is the abbreviation for daughter
the Jordan is a river in the Middle East; the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: A laid-off adviser confirms a lunch date with a daughter called Jordan.
explanation.walkthrough: Jordan looks like a girl's name in the surface but is the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger who offers unwanted advice to the driver is giving guidance nobody needs, hence superfluous advice.

clue.text: One Jerry avoids over in Majorca, the low-cost place to stay?

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the letters are read in the opposite order

parts.note: in the Tom and Jerry cartoons, Jerry the mouse is forever dodging Tom the cat
el is Spanish for 'the', and Majorca is a Spanish island

explanation.surface: A German tourist (a Jerry) skips a cheap Majorcan hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerry suggests the old slang for a German, but it is the cartoon mouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A motel is a roadside hotel for motorists, generally basic and inexpensive accommodation for a night.

clue.text: Dude with Stetson, say, and sunburn — out of place here?

parts.note: dude is slang for a man
a Stetson is a kind of cowboy hat
a tan is skin darkened by the sun

explanation.surface: A cowboy with his hat and weathered skin looks lost in the big city.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the place where such a cowboy would be out of place; it leans on the whole surface, and the question mark marks it as indirect.
explanation.definitionFit: Manhattan is the crowded heart of New York City, the last place a sunburnt ranch hand would blend in.

clue.text: Decline to back staff, retaining one that's full of energy

indicators.note: going back means going in reverse, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: to sag is to droop or decline

indicators.note: to retain is to hold on to something, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: to man is to staff, as in manning a desk
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to support an employee who happens to be bursting with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline to back' reads as refusing support but is SAG reversed. The definition borrows 'one' from the wordplay: one that's full of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas main is the large underground pipe carrying gas, a fuel, so it is filled with an energy source.

clue.text: Suspicion shellfish collection has put wife out

indicators.note: putting something out removes it, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: winkling is gathering winkles, small edible sea snails
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Someone suspects that a seafood collection has driven a wife out of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: A winkle is a small sea snail; gathering them is winkling, and the W comes off the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkling is a vague hint or slight notion that something is so, much like a hunch.

clue.text: Private line needed after unobtainable there

parts.note: a dish that is off is no longer available
taken as written
a cord is a line or string

explanation.surface: A private phone line is needed because the number there is unobtainable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the line at the end, following the other two pieces; 'line' and 'unobtainable' suggest a telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks made off the record are confidential and not for publication, so they stay unofficial and unreported.

clue.text: Put flags down after uplifting talk and disperse

indicators.note: in a vertical clue, lifting something means reading from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: flags are flagstones, so laying them is paving
to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: After an inspiring speech, the crowd lowers its banners and goes home.
explanation.walkthrough: Flags look like banners, but they are flagstones; 'uplifting' looks like praise for the talk but turns the paving upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaporate is to vanish or fade away, as liquid turns to vapour and scatters into the air.

clue.text: Covers notice about swallowing prunes

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside, so one piece goes into the other
turning about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to notice is to see
prunes as a verb: trims or clips

explanation.surface: A notice about eating dried plums.
explanation.walkthrough: Prunes look like the fruit but are a verb meaning cuts back.
explanation.definitionFit: When the moon eclipses the sun, it blocks it from view, so it obscures or hides it.

clue.text: Happen to get agitated about this compiler with variable inspiration

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece goes around another
something agitated is stirred and shaken, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
the setter refers to themself, so this compiler is me, I
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown values

explanation.surface: The setter gets worked up when a sudden, unpredictable idea arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This compiler' is the setter speaking of themself, giving I.
explanation.definitionFit: An epiphany is a sudden moment of insight or revelation, a flash of understanding that arrives unbidden.

clue.text: Plagiarise Constable as an example, with background drawn in by you once

parts.note: a police constable is an example of a cop

indicators.note: something drawn in is pulled inside, so pieces are placed within another

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of you
with means and, joining things together
a person's background is their past

explanation.surface: Copying a Constable landscape, with the background sketched in by someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable suggests John Constable the painter, which fits 'background drawn in', but it is a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To plagiarise is to pass off another's work as your own, which duplicating text and inserting it elsewhere does.

clue.text: Battle at sea — could one reduce suffering?

indicators.note: to be at sea is to be confused and lost, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A naval battle, and the question of whether anything could ease the pain of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' reads as the location of a naval battle but signals the mix-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is a pill, such as a painkiller, taken to ease pain or the symptoms of illness.

clue.text: Enjoys terrifically when it's shelled?

indicators.note: shelling something strips off its outside, leaving only the inner part of the words

parts.note: the letters span the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone loves a certain food, but only once its shell is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the instruction and the definition: remove the outer letters from the two words and you have a shellfish people relish once opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters are shellfish eaten after shucking, prized by many diners as a delicacy, so they are enjoyed once opened.

clue.text: One's favourite American drive

parts.note: one is I, and one's is read as one is, so I'M
a teacher's pet is the favourite
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Someone describing their preferred American road trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' reads as possessive but is taken as 'one is', I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the force or motivation pushing something forward, the push that makes things happen.

clue.text: Squalid recording on the radio

indicators.note: what is on the radio is heard rather than read, so the spoken form counts

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc, a recording

explanation.surface: A sleazy recording being played on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, the two letters of the compact disc abbreviation make the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy describes something sordid, shabby and disreputable, like a run-down bar or neighbourhood.

clue.text: Thy son, first appearing in the East?

definitions.text: Thy son, first appearing in the East?

indicators.note: on a map east is the right-hand side, so the opening letter moves to the end

parts.note: thy is the old form of your, and a son is a lad

explanation.surface: An address to Mary about her son, born in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the Y of YOUR LAD to the end gives the answer, and the whole clue also works as a description: the mother addressed, whose son was born in the East (the Magi came from there).
explanation.definitionFit: Our Lady is a Christian title of the Virgin Mary, mother of Jesus, addressed as 'thy' in prayers.

clue.text: Really a rush date to see regular show

parts.note: so means really, as in 'so good'
taken as written
to pop out is to rush out briefly
an era is a period of time, a date in history

explanation.surface: Someone is in a real hurry to get to a date in time for their usual programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Date' suggests a romantic meeting but stands for a period in history.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a serial drama broadcast several times a week, following the same characters for years.

clue.text: Very late, inebriated gentleman's gentleman

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very

indicators.note: someone inebriated is drunk and unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A well-to-do man's servant out very late and drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gentleman's gentleman' is a set phrase for a manservant, as in Jeeves to Bertie Wooster.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet is a personal manservant who looks after a man's clothes and needs, the role Jeeves fills.

clue.text: What's miles above capital of Edinburgh?

definitions.text: What's miles above capital of Edinburgh?

parts.note: the sky is far overhead

indicators.note: a capital is the large opening letter of a word, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of Edinburgh

explanation.surface: A riddle about what lies far north of the Scottish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue also describes the place: Skye is a Scottish island many miles north (above, on a map) of Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland's north-west coast, well north of Edinburgh on any map.

clue.text: One puts down style used by novelist?

parts.note: a type is a kind or style
a novelist is a writer

explanation.surface: An author's style is criticised by someone who belittles it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts down' suggests disparaging someone, but the definition means setting words on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A typewriter is a machine that prints characters onto paper, recording text as letters are struck.
